## How to review

2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?

4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.

10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.

## 1. The people who believed  (`#the-people-who-believed`)

Cited ayat: 10:98, 37:147-148

> **10:98** فَلَوْلَا كَانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ ءَامَنَتْ فَنَفَعَهَآ إِيمَٰنُهَآ إِلَّا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ لَمَّآ ءَامَنُوا۟ كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمْ عَذَابَ ٱلْخِزْىِ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَمَتَّعْنَٰهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

> **37:147** وَأَرْسَلْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰ مِا۟ئَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ
>
> **37:148** فَـَٔامَنُوا۟ فَمَتَّعْنَٰهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

### Claims

**c1** (10:98): The Quran asks why there was no town that believed so that its belief benefitted it, except the people of Yunus.

**c2** (10:98): When they believed, God removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world.

**c3** (10:98, 37:148): God gave them enjoyment for a while.

**c4** (37:147): Another passage says that God sent him to a hundred thousand or more.

**c5** (37:148): The same passage says that they believed, so God gave them enjoyment for a while.

### One-minute summary

The Quran says that, apart from the people of Yunus, no town believed so that its belief benefitted it [c1]. When they believed, God removed the punishment of disgrace from them and gave them enjoyment for a while [c2][c3].

### Complete story

The Quran asks why there was no town that believed so that its belief benefitted it, except the people of Yunus [c1]. When they believed, God removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world [c2]. God gave them enjoyment for a while [c3]. Another passage says that God sent him to a hundred thousand or more [c4]. The same passage says that they believed, so God gave them enjoyment for a while [c5].

### Deep study

- The Quran asks why there was no town that believed so that its belief benefitted it, except the people of Yunus (10:98) [c1].
- When they believed, God removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world (10:98) [c2].
- God gave them enjoyment for a while (10:98, 37:148) [c3].
- Another passage says that God sent him to a hundred thousand or more (37:147) [c4].
- The same passage says that they believed, so God gave them enjoyment for a while (37:148) [c5].

### Kids mode

The Quran says that the people of Yunus believed [c1][c5]. Because they believed, God took away their punishment and let them enjoy life for a while [c2][c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage treats belief that came while a warning was still near as something that benefitted the people of Yunus [c1][c2]. One reading is that the ayat hold up their belief as a case that could have been repeated by other towns [c1].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: where the town was, when this happened, who the people of Yunus were, or how long the enjoyment lasted; the ayat say a while.
- Not established: the number in 37:147 is stated as a hundred thousand or more by the ayah; the ayah does not say how it was counted, and the draft adds nothing to it.
- Not established: the ayat do not say what led them to believe or what the punishment would have been; they say that it was removed.
- Not established: the pronoun of he in 37:147 is not named in that ayah; the draft reads it as Yunus because 10:98 names the people of Yunus.
